subject: human ear
title: What If You Never Cleaned Your Ears?

scenes.text: What if you never cleaned your ears? For most people, nothing bad. Your ears clean themselves.
Earwax is made in the outer part of the ear canal, where it catches dust and dirt.
Every time you chew or talk, your jaw moves, and the skin in the canal slowly grows outward.
That carries old wax to the opening, where it dries, flakes off or washes away in the shower.
Cotton swabs mostly push wax deeper. Too much wax builds up in about 1 in 10 children and 1 in 20 adults.
After 65 it's far more common, between 19 and 65 percent. Then a doctor clears it. Your ear is a conveyor belt.

description:
What if you never cleaned your ears? For most people, nothing: chewing, jaw motion and skin growing outward carry old earwax to the opening, where it falls away.
According to the American Academy of Otolaryngology, impacted wax still affects about 1 in 10 children, 1 in 20 adults and 19 to 65 percent of people over 65. Cotton swabs mostly push wax back in. See a doctor if your ears feel blocked.

first_comment: Doctors say the ear canal is self-cleaning, yet about 12 million Americans a year see a doctor about earwax. Do you use cotton swabs?
